decisions.title: Ready for your close-up
decisions.situation: Jules points a phone camera at you. You can see yourself on the screen. Your nose deserves further investigation.

choices.label: Move right up to the lens
Wave at the small person on screen
Turn around at the crucial moment

result.title: Mostly nostril
result.body: Jules keeps the picture. It is a bold choice of composition.

journal.text: I gave Jules a very close view of my nose.

decisions.title: Encore! Encore!
decisions.situation: You bang a spoon on a bowl. It makes a brilliant noise. You would like to check that result another twenty times.

result.title: A short, loud career
result.body: You keep banging until you drop the spoon. You look very pleased with yourself.

journal.text: I discovered how much noise a spoon and a bowl could make.

decisions.title: A very close race
decisions.situation: Your shadow keeps reaching the wall before you. You try standing still. It has apparently thought of that too.

choices.label: Make it do a silly dance

result.title: An obedient rival
result.body: You stop trying to beat the shadow and give it increasingly ridiculous instructions.

journal.text: I made my shadow do a silly dance.

decisions.title: The museum has escaped
decisions.situation: You empty your pocket collection onto the table for Jules. Three stones. A leaf. A slug you thought was another leaf. The slug makes for the edge.

choices.label: Return the slug before it reaches the floor
Claim the slug lives here now

result.title: Please follow the shiny line
result.body: You describe the stones while Jules catches the slug on a leaf. Your only moving exhibit is removed halfway through the tour.

journal.text: I gave Jules a museum tour while a slug escaped from my pocket collection.

decisions.title: The bean is not thriving
decisions.situation: The class bean plant is dead. Léa asks why your progress chart still says “thriving”. You added a smiley face this morning.

choices.label: Write an honest report on its demise
Ask Léa where you went wrong
Give it an emotional farewell speech

result.title: A useful post-mortem
result.body: You record the dry soil and brown leaves. Léa gives credit for the observations, rather than your earlier optimism.

journal.text: I corrected my report about a dead classroom bean plant.

decisions.title: The handle is no longer involved
decisions.situation: You knock Jules’s favourite mug off the table. The handle leaves the rest of the mug. Nobody saw.

choices.label: Slide the evidence behind a plant

result.title: Bad news, delivered properly
result.body: Jules is disappointed about the mug and pleased you said something.

journal.text: I admitted breaking Jules’s mug.

decisions.title: Apparently this was cool
decisions.situation: Jules plays a song they loved at your age. There is a lengthy explanation of how nobody makes music properly anymore.

choices.label: Ask what it reminds them of

result.title: Before they were your parent
result.body: The story is better than expected. You learn something new about Jules.

journal.text: I listened to Jules’s old music and the story behind it.

decisions.title: A previous version of you
decisions.situation: Jules finds an old recording of you explaining how rain works. Your theory involves somebody emptying a bath above the clouds.

choices.label: Ask to keep the recording private

result.title: The expert stands corrected
result.body: You laugh at your explanation. Jules remembers the questions that came after it.

journal.text: I watched an old childhood recording with Jules.

decisions.title: One star. Still hungry.
decisions.situation: Gabriel drafts a fake restaurant review of the school canteen. It includes the phrase “structural pasta”.

result.title: Less funny, more useful
result.body: You keep the specific complaints and remove the insults. Jules helps pass it on.

journal.text: I helped Gabriel turn a canteen rant into useful feedback.

decisions.title: A complaint from past you
decisions.situation: You find a childhood letter addressed to yourself. It says, “If you are not a dinosaur by thirteen, you have ruined everything.” There is a drawing of the expected dinosaur.

choices.label: Make a tail out of socks and deliver a roar
Write a formal rejection on the back

result.title: Partial compliance
result.body: The tail falls off during your first turn. You add “technical difficulties” beneath the original demand and draw yourself with better knees.

journal.text: I answered a childhood demand to become a dinosaur by making a sock tail.

decisions.title: Immortal words, wrong person
decisions.situation: The yearbook proof puts Gabriel’s quote under your photo: “I peaked at nine.” Jules needs corrections today. You are not sure you want to ask what happened at nine.

choices.label: Return the quote to its rightful owner
Approve it as your mysterious backstory

result.title: A corrected confession
result.body: Jules fixes the names. Gabriel explains that they won a particularly good sack race.

journal.text: I corrected swapped yearbook quotations.

decisions.title: Forwarded with absolutely no evidence
decisions.situation: A group chat is circulating an embarrassing rumour about someone your age. The source appears to be “everyone knows”.

result.title: An inconvenient question
result.body: Nobody produces evidence. The conversation changes topic with suspicious speed.

journal.text: I challenged a rumour in a group chat.

decisions.title: The microphone is still on
decisions.situation: After a class announcement, Gabriel whispers that the school jingle sounds like a microwave. The microphone is still on.

choices.label: Switch it off and warn them

result.title: Broadcast ends
result.body: Most people heard the first comment. You prevent a second one.

journal.text: I switched off a live microphone before Gabriel said anything worse.

decisions.title: Your shoulders have a complaint
decisions.situation: After sitting in the same position for a while, you notice that your shoulders appear to have crept up towards your ears.

choices.label: Change your position and relax your shoulders

result.title: A different position helps
result.body: You loosen up at a comfortable pace and return to what you were doing. You had not noticed how stiff you were.

journal.text: I took a gentle movement break after sitting still.

decisions.title: Practice grief
decisions.situation: At a free estate-planning demonstration, volunteers act as fictional heirs. Your card says “loving relative”. The person beside you is already asking what the imaginary house is worth.

choices.label: Ask how real inheritance rules work
Demand the imaginary house in character

result.title: A family worth inventing
result.body: You deliver a moving line about the fictional deceased. The facilitator thanks you. Your neighbour asks whether the line helped your share.

journal.text: I played a grieving relative at an estate-planning demonstration.

decisions.title: Water with a personal brand
decisions.situation: At a free tasting, a presenter claims their water has been “emotionally filtered”. The jug beside it is labelled TAP. You are just thirsty.

choices.label: Ask which emotions the filter removes
Debate the emotional lives of liquids

result.title: No emotional processing required
result.body: It tastes like water. The presenter watches you finish a glass with the expression of someone witnessing sabotage.

journal.text: I chose tap water at a premium-water demonstration.

decisions.title: Inner peace is on hold
decisions.situation: At a free relaxation class, the instructor tells you to release your anger. Their phone rings. They spend the next minute shouting at a printer repair company.

choices.label: Close your eyes and let them finish
Find peace on a walk outside
Offer to fix the printer problem

result.title: A guided loss of temper
result.body: You breathe slowly through an argument about toner. By the time they hang up, you are considerably calmer than the professional.

journal.text: I relaxed through my relaxation instructor’s furious printer call.

decisions.title: A shortcut through the execution
decisions.situation: A museum shortcut in Marseille takes you through a medieval punishment exhibit. A mechanical executioner swings a foam axe across the marked path. The long route has no executioner.

choices.label: Time the swing and walk through slowly
Sprint straight through the swinging axe

result.title: A head start
result.body: You turn back. A speaker announces, “The coward flees!” Three visitors turn to look. You continue with your head and your dignity approximately intact.

journal.text: I took the long route around a museum’s mechanical executioner.

decisions.title: The sofa is judging you
decisions.situation: Autoplay follows your programme with a competitive fitness class. A man who appears to have been assembled entirely from elbows challenges you to beat your personal best.

choices.label: Switch to the beginner version and try it
Keep up with him at full speed

result.title: An achievable number of elbows
result.body: You complete the gentler routine. The instructor says anyone can do it, then folds himself into a shape you decline to investigate.

journal.text: I followed a beginner workout after a fitness video appeared on autoplay.

decisions.title: The compliment has the wrong address
decisions.situation: Someone praises an anonymous poem you were standing beside at a free exhibition. You did not write it. They are waiting for you to explain its “raw emotional honesty”.

choices.label: Thank them, then admit it is not yours
Point out the actual poet’s name
Accept the praise and invent your inspiration

result.title: A narrow escape from poetry
result.body: They laugh at the mix-up. You both admit you were not entirely sure what the last line meant.

journal.text: I corrected a stranger who thought I had written a poem.

decisions.title: Water with a personal brand
decisions.situation: At a free tasting, a presenter claims their water has been “emotionally filtered”. The jug beside it is labelled TAP. You are just thirsty.

choices.label: Ask which emotions the filter removes
Debate the emotional lives of liquids

result.title: No emotional processing required
result.body: It tastes like water. The presenter watches you finish a glass with the expression of someone witnessing sabotage.

journal.text: I chose tap water at a premium-water demonstration.

decisions.title: Doing nothing, attendance required
decisions.situation: You put “Do absolutely nothing” in your calendar. The app sends invitations to a discussion group. Six people accept and one asks about the dress code.

choices.label: Cancel it and protect your hour
Host exactly five minutes of nothing
Send an agenda for competitive relaxing

result.title: A successful cancellation
result.body: You explain that it was private. Someone replies that they were really looking forward to nothing. You enjoy it without them.

journal.text: I cancelled accidental invitations to my free hour.

decisions.title: One missed intention
decisions.situation: You miss a small personal intention and catch yourself declaring the whole effort ruined. The declaration is much larger than the missed step.

choices.label: Ask whether the intention needs adjusting

result.title: A smaller conclusion
result.body: You treat the missed moment as one moment and carry on with what you can manage now.

journal.text: I avoided turning a small missed intention into a verdict on everything.

decisions.title: The quiet place has noises
decisions.situation: You sit somewhere quiet and immediately notice a clock, a distant door and somebody clearing their throat. Apparently quiet did not mean perfectly silent.

choices.label: Let the ordinary sounds be there
Choose one steady sound to notice

result.title: Quiet enough is available
result.body: You stop checking each sound for a reason to be irritated. The place becomes restful without becoming silent.

journal.text: I accepted ordinary background sounds in a quiet moment.

decisions.title: Inside the chicken
decisions.situation: The festival mascot has quit. A volunteer thrusts a chicken suit at you and offers cash for one hour. The head smells of onions. Something inside it is still warm.

choices.label: Tell them you only came for the stalls
Carry the head around and ask if anyone knows it

result.title: A civilian again
result.body: The volunteer apologises and puts the chicken head on a traffic cone. A child immediately asks the cone for a photo.

journal.text: I declined an emergency shift inside a festival chicken.

decisions.title: One more attempt at your name
decisions.situation: At a local discussion group, the host mispronounces your name twice and then suggests a nickname you have never used.

choices.label: Say your name clearly once more
Turn the correction into a light joke
Use the nickname for the afternoon

result.title: A manageable correction
result.body: The host repeats it correctly and moves on. The proposed nickname retires before its first appearance.

journal.text: I corrected my name instead of accepting an unwanted nickname.

decisions.title: The missing letter
decisions.situation: A poster for a free public cookery class has dropped the L from “public”. The organiser cannot work out why people keep arriving with suspicious questions.

choices.label: Point out the missing letter quietly
Leave the organiser to discover it
Read the heading aloud to the queue

result.title: A little tape saves the afternoon
result.body: The organiser repairs the heading and looks at the queue with fresh concern. The class returns to soup.

journal.text: I pointed out an embarrassing typo on a cookery-class poster.

decisions.title: The accidental millionaire
decisions.situation: At a charity auction, someone mistakes you for a wealthy donor. The auctioneer hands you the microphone beside a photograph of an elderly donkey. “How much will you give?” The room goes quiet.

choices.label: Admit your wealth has been exaggerated
Claim you are the donkey’s lawyer

result.title: A donkey-sized misunderstanding
result.body: You explain that you were looking for the toilets. The auctioneer takes back the microphone and points down the corridor. Several people applaud your honesty. One applauds the donkey.

journal.text: I admitted I was not the wealthy donor a charity auction expected.

decisions.title: Nothing to worry about
decisions.situation: At a free repair demonstration, a wind-up toy starts smoking. The volunteer explains that it is supposed to do that. The label “DO NOT WIND” drops off its base.

choices.label: Step back and let them stop it

result.title: A useful admission
result.body: The volunteer stops and explains the failed mechanism. You learn more from the mistake than from the planned demonstration.

journal.text: I asked about a warning label during a failed toy-repair demonstration.

decisions.title: Everyone here is a winner
decisions.situation: At a motivational taster session, you are asked to name your greatest achievement. The person before you says they survived eight workplace investigations. The facilitator applauds and turns to you.

choices.label: Say you got out of bed today
Ask what the investigations were about

result.title: A standing achievement
result.body: The facilitator calls this a triumph over horizontal thinking. Everyone stands to applaud. You sit down before they can invent a course about it.

journal.text: I told a motivational group that getting out of bed was my achievement.

decisions.title: A striking resemblance
decisions.situation: A caricaturist at a street fair in Marseille offers you a free sample portrait. A small crowd gathers. The artist turns the drawing around. It is you as an enormous angry thumb.

choices.label: Ask whether they could add a jawline
Ask for a pencil and draw the artist

result.title: The formal thumb
result.body: The artist adds a bow tie. You point out that this is not a jawline. A spectator says the resemblance is uncanny. You leave holding a thumb in evening wear.

journal.text: I asked a caricaturist to correct my portrait and received a thumb in a bow tie.

decisions.title: Your murderous past
decisions.situation: A walking-tour guide points straight at you and tells the group you are the ghost of a notorious murderer. You are outside a shop in Marseille, holding a sandwich.

choices.label: Explain that you are alive and eating lunch
Ask what crimes you supposedly committed
Follow the tour without breaking eye contact

result.title: New evidence
result.body: The guide calls your sandwich an unsettling detail. You take a large bite. A tourist asks whether ghosts can eat cheese. The guide moves the group along.

journal.text: I corrected a walking tour that mistook me for a murderer’s ghost in Marseille.

journal.text: I ignored an unhelpful achievement list on my birthday.

decisions.title: A complaint from your younger self
decisions.situation: You find a note from your younger self: By fifty-five, we will be independently wealthy and know how to fold a fitted sheet. The handwriting is extremely confident.

choices.label: Send your younger self a furious reply

result.title: The corners remain hostile
result.body: You report that the elastic corners remain a problem. You omit finances; you are not being interrogated by a child with a felt-tip pen.

journal.text: I answered an old note about being wealthy and folding fitted sheets.

decisions.title: It cannot have been this bad
decisions.situation: You revisit a comedy you have called your favourite for years. Ten minutes in, a man falls into a bucket for the fourth time. You appear to have remembered a much better programme.

choices.label: Work out what you used to enjoy
Watch the whole thing out of loyalty

result.title: The bucket loses a fan
result.body: You stop watching without trying to defend your younger self in court. There are other ways to spend the evening.

journal.text: I stopped pretending to enjoy an old favourite programme.

decisions.title: How much do you want to explain?
decisions.situation: Someone asks for details about your experience of Hypertension. They sound concerned, but you are not sure you want to have the whole conversation.

choices.label: Say which part you are comfortable sharing
Share more because talking feels helpful

result.title: Your information stays yours
result.body: You give the amount of explanation you choose. Concern does not entitle another person to every detail.

journal.text: I set a clear boundary around discussing Hypertension.

decisions.title: A few words from our guest
decisions.situation: At a free local event, the host hands you a microphone and thanks you for “everything you did”. You have no idea what you allegedly did.

choices.label: Ask what you are being thanked for
Thank everyone who made this possible

result.title: The right person is found
result.body: You were mistaken for the person who fixed a blocked toilet. Their arrival receives the applause they earned.

journal.text: I corrected a mistaken public thank-you before giving a speech.
